shapes/relu: Three activations do most of the work. The ReLU keeps positive numbers and zeroes the rest: ReLU of two is two, and ReLU of minus two is zero.
shapes/sigmoid: The sigmoid squashes any number into the range from zero to one. Sigmoid of zero is a half, and of two, about zero point eight eight. Of minus two, it is one minus that: zero point one two.
shapes/tanh: tan-aitch squashes into the range from minus one to one, centered on zero: tan-aitch of zero is zero. tan-aitch of one is about zero point seven six, and tan-aitch of minus one is minus zero point seven six.
shapes/ranges: So the ReLU's outputs run from zero up with no limit: zero to infinity, where infinity means no end. A square bracket includes its end, and a round one never reaches it. The sigmoid's outputs lie in zero to one, and tan-aitch's in minus one to one.
slopes/d-relu: Backprop needs each one's slope. The ReLU's is the simplest: one where its input is positive, and zero where it is negative.
slopes/d-sig: The sigmoid's slope is sigma times one minus sigma. At zero that is a half times a half: a quarter, the most it ever gets. At two, zero point eight eight times zero point one two: about zero point one.
slopes/nudge: For tan-aitch, nudge the input and watch the output. From zero to zero point zero one, tan-aitch moves by the same zero point zero one: a slope of one. From one to one point zero one, it moves by only about zero point zero zero four two: a slope of zero point four two.
slopes/d-tanh: Both fit one rule: tan-aitch's slope is one minus tan-aitch squared. At zero, tan-aitch is zero, so the slope is one minus zero squared: one, its most. At one, it is one minus zero point seven six squared, which is one minus zero point five eight: about zero point four two.
slopes/flat: Far from zero, both squashing curves go flat, and their slopes sink toward zero. A unit stuck out there is saturated: almost no gradient gets through it.
why/chain: Chain several units one after another, and backprop multiplies the gradient by one slope per link. Through five sigmoids, that is at most a quarter, five times over: about one thousandth.
why/whole: Through five ReLUs that are on, it is one, five times: the gradient arrives whole. That is the main reason ReLU became the default.
why/dead: The catch is the dead ReLU. A unit whose pre-activation is negative for every input it sees has a slope of zero every time, so no gradient ever reaches the weights feeding it.
